subject: general
question: The curved surface area of a cylinder is half of its total surface area. If its height is 10 cm, then find the volume of the cylinder (in cm³).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If **Curved Surface Area (CSA)** is half of **Total Surface Area (TSA)**, then **CSA = Area of 2 bases**.

2πrh = 2πr² ⇒ **h = r**.

Given **height (h) = 10 cm**, so **radius (r) = 10 cm**.

**Volume = πr²h** = π × 10² × 10 = 1000π cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 1000π cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Height (h) = 10 cm; CSA = 1/2 × TSA.

**Formula Used:** CSA = 2πrh; TSA = 2πr(h + r); Volume = πr²h.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3c46d640ac2b089d06f0b5537c03f4c3ed22f26c6803ac19f57c7b15bac63f29.png] 

⇒ 2πrh = 1/2 × [2πr(h + r)]

⇒ 2πrh = πr(h + r)

⇒ 2h = h + r

⇒ 2h − h = r ⇒ **r = h**

⇒ r = 10 cm

⇒ Volume = π × (10)² × 10

⇒ Volume = π × 100 × 10 = 1000π cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 1000π cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Surface Area of Cylinder

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πrh and Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2πr(h + r).

Volume of Cylinder

The space occupied is given by Volume = πr²h.

Ratio of CSA to TSA

The ratio is h : (h + r). In this specific case, 1 : 2 implies h = r.</p
